newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold down on overseas sales pressure. [CORRECTED 10:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold down on overseas sales pressure. [CORRECTED 10:30 GMT]

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed down from New York on Friday on selling pressure from overseas, gold dealers and traders said.
Bullion ended at US$382.30/382.80 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$382.85/383.25 close on Thursday (corrects from Monday).
Local gold ended HK$12 lower at HK$3,524 a tael.
Morning trade was uneventful with continued light gold sales from the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) as the yen remained weak, dealers said.
Unable to break $384, gold hovered around $383.90, where some selling kicked in from overseas, but the metal has held at $382.30-382.60, gold dealers said.

At the opening, traders were offering prices slightly below the market level but nothing was traded until Europe opened, and professional selling interest was strong enough to take up those offers, said one gold trader at a bullion firm.
A prediction that European central banks may sell more of their gold holdings also contributed to eager sales by overseas customers, some gold dealers said.

N.M. Rothschild and Sons Ltd director Robert Guy said at the Nikkei Gold Conference in Tokyo on Friday that European central banks may sell more gold holdings in the future amid pressure to reduce budget deficits as European monetary union proceeds.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society was at -5, down from its previous fix at -0.10.
